title: feat(dialect): Add Continue.dev adapter (.continue/prompts/*.prompt & slash commands)
body:
## Problem Statement / Background

Continue.dev is the most widely adopted open-source AI coding assistant in VS Code and JetBrains IDEs. Developers want to reuse their Cinch skills inside Continue as native custom slash commands and prompt templates.
Currently, users must manually copy markdown files into `.continue/prompts/` and adapt prompt variables.

## Inspiration from State-of-the-Art Tools

Continue.dev defines `.prompt` files with frontmatter specifying `name`, `description`, `invocable`, and handlebars-style context variables (`{{{ input }}}`, `{{{ current_file }}}`).

## Proposed Solution & Architecture

Implement `src/cinch/dialects/continue_dev.py`:
1. Compile Cinch skills to `.continue/prompts/<skill_name>.prompt`.
2. Translate standard Cinch frontmatter (`description`, `paths`, `variables`) into Continue's prompt schema.
3. Register command shortcuts in `.continue/config.json` if present.
4. Add conformance tests in `tests/test_dialects/test_continue.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria & Test Plan

- [ ] `cinch sync --target continue` outputs valid `.continue/prompts/<name>.prompt`.
- [ ] Handles variable substitutions without breaking Handlebars syntax.
- [ ] Conformance tests verify generated prompt files.
- [ ] Documentation updated in README harness matrix.

title: feat(sync): Live file watcher daemon (`cinch watch`) for instantaneous cross-editor sync
body:
## Problem Statement / Background

Developers frequently iterate on skill prompts and agent rules. Running `cinch sync` manually after every markdown edit slows down the development feedback loop across multiple open IDEs (e.g. Cursor, Claude Code, Zed, VS Code).

## Inspiration from State-of-the-Art Tools

Modern developer tooling like `cargo watch`, `tailwind --watch`, and `astro dev` use low-overhead OS file event notifications (via `watchfiles` or `kqueue`/`inotify`) to debounce and recompile artifacts in $<10\text{ms}$.

## Proposed Solution & Architecture

Implement `cinch watch [--target <name>] [--debounce <ms>]`:
1. Monitor source skill directories (`.skills/` or configured paths) for create/modify/delete events.
2. Debounce file change events by 150ms to prevent duplicate builds on atomic editor saves.
3. Incremental recompilation: only re-compile and write the modified skill dialect file rather than the entire workspace.
4. Clean ANSI status line showing updated files and execution time.

## Acceptance Criteria & Test Plan

- [ ] `cinch watch` starts a non-blocking daemon listening to file changes.
- [ ] Edits to a source skill update target harness files within 50ms.
- [ ] Graceful termination on `SIGINT` / `Ctrl+C`.
- [ ] Unit tests using temporary directory watcher mock.

title: feat(import): Reverse-sync engine (`cinch import`) to decompile legacy .cursorrules & .claude/skills
body:
## Problem Statement / Background

Teams already have dozens of bespoke `.cursorrules`, `.clinerules`, Copilot instructions, and `.claude/skills/` spread across legacy repositories. Adopting Cinch currently requires manually migrating each file into Cinch's universal format.

## Inspiration from State-of-the-Art Tools

`pandoc` and `ast-grep` allow bidirectional translation between AST representations. Migration tools like `migrate-workflows` parse legacy configurations and extract structured metadata into modern canonical specs.

## Proposed Solution & Architecture

Implement `cinch import <path_or_preset>`:
1. Auto-detect source dialect based on path (`.cursorrules`, `.clinerules`, `.claude/skills/*`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`).
2. Extract system instructions, triggers, globs, and tool descriptions.
3. Normalize into canonical Cinch markdown with standard YAML frontmatter.
4. Dry-run diff preview before writing.

## Acceptance Criteria & Test Plan

- [ ] Successfully decompiles `.cursorrules` and `.clinerules` into valid Cinch skills.
- [ ] Preserves all instructions, formatting, and markdown links.
- [ ] Round-trip assertion: `import(export(skill)) == skill`.
- [ ] Unit tests covering each supported legacy dialect.

title: feat(lint): Strict JSON Schema & Pydantic validation for skill frontmatter (`cinch check --strict`)
body:
## Problem Statement / Background

Malformed frontmatter (invalid YAML syntax, missing `description`, unrecognized keys, bad glob syntax in `paths`) silently breaks client harnesses like Claude Code and Windsurf at runtime.

## Inspiration from State-of-the-Art Tools

`actionlint` and `yamllint` catch syntax and schema errors before CI deployment, giving precise line and column error diagnostics with friendly suggestions.

## Proposed Solution & Architecture

1. Define a strict Pydantic model (`SkillManifestSchema`) in `src/cinch/schema.py`.
2. Validate required fields (`name`, `description`), optional metadata (`version`, `author`, `license`), and dialect-specific rules (`paths` glob validity, max description lengths for Cursor/Windsurf).
3. Enhance `cinch check` to report colored error diagnostics with file paths, line numbers, and actionable remediation steps.

## Acceptance Criteria & Test Plan

- [ ] `cinch check` detects invalid YAML, missing keys, and invalid glob patterns.
- [ ] Returns non-zero exit code on errors for CI integration.
- [ ] Helpful hints on misspelled keys (e.g. `desc` -> `description`).
- [ ] Comprehensive test suite in `tests/test_check.py`.

title: feat(tui): Interactive terminal catalog & previewer (`cinch tui`) built with Textual
body:
## Problem Statement / Background

Developers managing large skill collections need an intuitive way to browse installed skills, preview how a skill compiles into different client dialects side-by-side, and toggle harnesses interactively.

## Inspiration from State-of-the-Art Tools

Modern developer TUIs like `lazygit`, `gh dash`, and `posting` provide immediate, keyboard-driven exploration of complex configurations without leaving the terminal.

## Proposed Solution & Architecture

Implement `cinch tui`:
1. Left panel: List of all discovered skills with tags, dialect support icons, and filter search bar.
2. Top-right panel: Markdown preview of the selected skill source.
3. Bottom-right panel: Live compilation diff showing the output for any selected harness dialect (Cursor, Claude Code, Windsurf, Copilot, Continue).
4. Keybindings: `j/k` navigation, `/` search, `s` sync, `q` quit.

## Acceptance Criteria & Test Plan

- [ ] Launchable via `cinch tui` with optional dependency check (prompting install of `textual` or bundled).
- [ ] Live preview updates instantly when switching dialect tabs.
- [ ] Graceful fallback if terminal is non-interactive or too small.

title: feat(security): Zero-leak secret & token scanner in `cinch check --audit-secrets`
body:
## Problem Statement / Background

Prompts and skill instructions often inadvertently contain sensitive credentials (API keys, bearer tokens, internal staging URLs, absolute user paths `/Users/alice/...`). When skills are exported or committed to public repositories, these secrets leak.

## Inspiration from State-of-the-Art Tools

Tools like `gitleaks`, `trufflehog`, and `detect-secrets` scan text using high-entropy detectors and regex signatures for 100+ known API provider patterns (OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS, GitHub tokens).

## Proposed Solution & Architecture

Add `cinch check --audit-secrets`:
1. Standard library regex engine matching known token formats (`sk-...`, `ghp_...`, `Bearer ...`, AWS keys).
2. Shannon entropy analysis to catch high-entropy base64/hex strings in prompts.
3. Detect hardcoded local user directories (`/Users/...`, `C:\Users\...`).
4. Redaction mode (`cinch sync --redact-secrets`) that replaces detected secrets with placeholder environment variable references (`${API_KEY}`).

## Acceptance Criteria & Test Plan

- [ ] Flags common API key formats and high-entropy secrets in skills.
- [ ] Zero false alarms on standard code examples and markdown code fences.
- [ ] Fails `cinch check --audit-secrets` with exit code 1 if credentials are discovered.
- [ ] Unit tests covering positive and negative secret detection.

title: feat(bridge): Dynamic MCP server schema bridge (`cinch bridge mcp`)
body:
## Problem Statement / Background

Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers expose rich tools and resources. However, many harnesses (like Claude Code skills, Copilot workspace, or Cursor rules) benefit from prompt-based skills that guide the agent on *when* and *how* to invoke these MCP tools effectively.

## Inspiration from State-of-the-Art Tools

`mcp-cli` and Anthropic's Model Context Protocol reference inspectors query server tools via JSON-RPC `tools/list`.

## Proposed Solution & Architecture

Implement `cinch bridge mcp <command>` or `cinch bridge mcp --config mcp.json`:
1. Spawn the specified MCP server subprocess and call `tools/list` via JSON-RPC STDIO.
2. Synthesize clean, documented Cinch skills wrapping each tool or tool cluster.
3. Embed input schemas, argument constraints, and few-shot usage examples into the skill instructions.
4. Output generated skills to `.skills/mcp-<server>/`.

## Acceptance Criteria & Test Plan

- [ ] Introspects stdio MCP servers and retrieves tool manifests.
- [ ] Generates valid, high-quality Cinch skills documenting tool execution.
- [ ] Handles tool parameter descriptions and required vs optional arguments cleanly.
- [ ] Unit tests with a mocked MCP stdio server.

title: feat(html): Standalone searchable single-file HTML & documentation catalog generator
body:
## Problem Statement / Background

Engineering teams and open-source projects need to share their catalog of AI skills with colleagues and contributors who may not have Python or Cinch installed locally.

## Inspiration from State-of-the-Art Tools

Tools like `repomix`, `redoc`, and `dbt docs generate` output single-file, zero-dependency HTML artifacts with embedded search, dark mode, and responsive layout that can be hosted on GitHub Pages or shared in Slack.

## Proposed Solution & Architecture

Implement `cinch export --format html --output docs/skills.html`:
1. Bundle all skills into a standalone, single HTML file (CSS & JS inlined, no CDN dependencies).
2. Searchable skill cards with keyword filtering, tag badges, and dialect compatibility pills.
3. One-click "Copy Prompt" and "Copy for Claude/Cursor" clipboard buttons.
4. Responsive layout with dark/light mode toggle.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Produces single self-contained HTML file $<500\text{KB}$.
- [ ] Client-side instant fuzzy search across titles, descriptions, and prompt bodies.
- [ ] Operates 100% offline without external network requests.
- [ ] Tested across modern web browsers.

title: feat(composer): Skill composition & DAG dependency chaining (`requires: [skill1, skill2]`)
body:
## Problem Statement / Background

Complex agent tasks require combining multiple primitive skills (e.g. `git-pr-flow` requires `test-runner` and `semantic-commit`). Currently, authors must duplicate instructions across skills, causing prompt bloat and synchronization issues.

## Inspiration from State-of-the-Art Tools

`ansible` roles, `terraform` modules, and GitHub Actions `composite` actions allow modular composition with dependency resolution and deduplication.

## Proposed Solution & Architecture

1. Support `requires: [skill_a, skill_b]` in Cinch skill frontmatter.
2. Implement a topological sort dependency resolver in `src/cinch/resolver.py`.
3. Cycle detection with descriptive circular dependency error messages.
4. Automated deduplication when compiling multi-skill agent bundles, ensuring shared sub-skills are included only once.

## Acceptance Criteria & Test Plan

- [ ] Topological resolution of skill dependency trees.
- [ ] Emits clear error on cyclic dependencies (`A -> B -> A`).
- [ ] Deduplicates shared prerequisites in dialect exports.
- [ ] Full unit test coverage in `tests/test_resolver.py`.

title: feat(params): Parameterized skills with interactive CLI input wizard & template interpolation
body:
## Problem Statement / Background

Many skills require project-specific inputs (e.g., target staging URL, database branch, test coverage threshold). Hardcoding these in static markdown forces teams to create duplicated variations of the same skill.

## Inspiration from State-of-the-Art Tools

`cookiecutter`, `copier`, and `jinja2` allow declarative parameter schemas with default values, validation regexes, and interactive prompts.

## Proposed Solution & Architecture

1. Support `parameters` block in frontmatter:
   ```yaml
   parameters:
     min_coverage: { type: int, default: 80, help: "Minimum test coverage %" }
     framework: { type: string, choices: [pytest, jest, vitest] }
   ```
2. When running or compiling with `cinch sync --interactive`, prompt the developer for values or load from `.cinch.env`.
3. Render variables using safe stdlib string templates or Jinja2 syntax.

## Acceptance Criteria & Test Plan

- [ ] Schema validation for typed parameters (string, int, boolean, choice).
- [ ] Interactive prompts in terminal when parameters are unset.
- [ ] Support parameter overrides via CLI flags (`--param min_coverage=90`) and environment variables.
- [ ] Unit tests for template rendering.

title: feat(dialect): Add Zed editor slash commands & context server adapter (.zed/prompts/)
body:
## Problem Statement / Background

Zed is rapidly gaining traction among developers due to its blazing-fast GPU-accelerated Rust editor and built-in AI Assistant panel. Developers want their Cinch skills available in Zed.

## Inspiration from State-of-the-Art Tools

Zed AI supports custom prompts stored in `.zed/prompts/` and slash commands that inject context into conversational threads.

## Proposed Solution & Architecture

Implement `src/cinch/dialects/zed.py`:
1. Compile Cinch skills to `.zed/prompts/<skill_name>.md`.
2. Format system instructions for Zed's assistant context model.
3. Document Zed configuration and keyboard shortcuts in Cinch documentation.

## Acceptance Criteria & Test Plan

- [ ] `cinch sync --target zed` generates valid `.zed/prompts/` files.
- [ ] Conformance tests in `tests/test_dialects/test_zed.py`.
- [ ] Verification with Zed editor prompt schema.

title: feat(diff): Semantic prompt diffing (`cinch diff`) across git revisions and dialects
body:
## Problem Statement / Background

When updating a skill prompt or refactoring instructions, maintainers need to know: *"How does this edit impact the compiled output across all 9 harnesses? Did the tokens increase? Did frontmatter metadata change?"*

## Inspiration from State-of-the-Art Tools

`git diff`, `difftastic`, and `pkgdiff` compute structural and semantic diffs showing exact syntactic alterations rather than raw text line changes.

## Proposed Solution & Architecture

Implement `cinch diff [git-ref] [--dialect <name>]`:
1. Compare current local skills against `git-ref` (e.g. `main` or `HEAD~1`) or compare source skill vs compiled dialect.
2. Display colored side-by-side terminal diff showing frontmatter changes, body modifications, and token delta.
3. Support `--stat` flag showing total token count changes across all harnesses.

## Acceptance Criteria & Test Plan

- [ ] `cinch diff` displays clear, readable terminal diffs.
- [ ] Reports token count deltas ($\\pm N$ tokens).
- [ ] Works cleanly inside git worktrees.
- [ ] Unit tests in `tests/test_diff.py`.

title: feat(bench): Multi-model token cost & footprint benchmark harness (`cinch bench`)
body:
## Problem Statement / Background

Prompts are injected into context windows on every user turn. Bloated skills cost money and degrade LLM reasoning performance. Cinch currently has a microsecond speed benchmark, but lacks an automated token footprint profiler across target LLM tokenizers.

## Inspiration from State-of-the-Art Tools

`tiktoken`, UsageTrim, and `tokencounter` calculate exact token encodings for GPT-4, Claude 3, Llama 3, and Gemini tokenizers.

## Proposed Solution & Architecture

Add `cinch bench [--tokens] [--pricing baseline.json]`:
1. Calculate exact token consumption per skill across Claude (`cl100k`), OpenAI (`o200k`), and Gemini tokenizers.
2. Compute dollar cost per 1,000 invocations based on current vendor API pricing.
3. Highlight skills exceeding configurable token thresholds ($>800$ tokens).
4. Export benchmark metrics as structured JSON for CI regression checks.

## Acceptance Criteria & Test Plan

- [ ] Computes exact token count and dollar cost per dialect.
- [ ] Fails CI if any skill exceeds the configured token budget.
- [ ] Zero runtime crash if optional tokenizer dependencies are missing (graceful heuristic fallback).
- [ ] Unit tests in `tests/test_benchmarks.py`.

title: feat(package): Git-native remote skill package manager (`cinch install gh:owner/repo@v1`)
body:
## Problem Statement / Background

Organizations want to share standard skill libraries (e.g. corporate security rules, team coding conventions) without copy-pasting markdown files between repositories.

## Inspiration from State-of-the-Art Tools

`brew`, `uv`, and `kustomize` allow remote package installation from GitHub repositories with tag pinning, checksum verification, and lockfiles.

## Proposed Solution & Architecture

Implement `cinch install <git_url_or_shorthand>` and `cinch update`:
1. Fetch remote skills from git repositories (`gh:org/skills@v1.2.0`).
2. Verify integrity and record dependency pins in `cinch.lock`.
3. Vendor remote skills into `.skills/vendor/<name>/`.
4. Support clean uninstallation via `cinch uninstall <name>`.

## Acceptance Criteria & Test Plan

- [ ] Installs skills from public and private GitHub repositories.
- [ ] Deterministic version pinning via `cinch.lock`.
- [ ] Offline caching in `~/.cache/cinch/`.
- [ ] Unit tests with local git fixture repositories.

title: feat(eval): Automated skill assertion & prompt regression test runner (`cinch eval`)
body:
## Problem Statement / Background

When authoring or modifying skills, maintainers have no way to automatically test whether the prompt actually guides the AI model to perform the expected actions (e.g. generating the right tool calls, following formatting instructions, not hallucinating invalid flags).

## Inspiration from State-of-the-Art Tools

`promptfoo`, `deepeval`, and `evals` provide declarative assertion testing for LLM prompts using schema validation and deterministic assertions.

## Proposed Solution & Architecture

Implement `cinch eval [skill_name]`:
1. Define test fixtures in `evals/<skill>.eval.yml`:
   ```yaml
   tests:
     - vars: { input: "Fix pytest failure" }
       assert:
         - contains: "pytest -v"
         - not_contains: "sudo rm -rf"
   ```
2. Execute offline deterministic assertions (regex, JSON Schema, keyword checks) or optional live LLM evaluation via API.
3. Output test results in standard JUnit XML for CI pipelines.

## Acceptance Criteria & Test Plan

- [ ] Evaluates skills against declarative assertions without requiring external API keys for static checks.
- [ ] JUnit XML output for GitHub Actions test reporting.
- [ ] Passes/fails with standard exit codes.
- [ ] Full unit test coverage in `tests/test_eval.py`.
